message: 55M. My right hand has been numb and tingly for a few days, worse at night. No weakness anywhere, no face drooping, my speech is normal.

output.patientMessage: You can manage this at home for now. Numbness and tingling in one hand that is worse at night, without weakness or speech change, commonly comes from nerve compression at the wrist. If you develop sudden face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking, call 911 right away. If hand weakness, dropping objects, or loss of feeling develops or symptoms persist or worsen over the next couple of weeks, arrange a clinician assessment; if you cannot get one, use an urgent care clinic.

edits.value: Right hand numbness and tingling for a few days, worse at night, with denied weakness, facial droop and speech change fits a common compressive hand neuropathy pattern; onset character is unreported, so the message directs immediate emergency assessment if the numbness started abruptly, and otherwise no clinician assessment, prescribing or testing is established as needed now.

First: if this numbness came on abruptly, all at once, go to an emergency department now for urgent assessment, even without weakness or speech change. If instead it built up gradually, you can manage it at home for now — hand numbness and tingling worse at night often comes from nerve compression at the wrist. If you develop sudden face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking, call 911 right away. If hand weakness, dropping objects or loss of feeling develops, or symptoms persist or worsen over the next couple of weeks, arrange a clinician assessment; if you cannot get one, use an urgent care clinic.
